definition: All query heads share a single key/value head, shrinking the KV cache dramatically and speeding up decoding at a small quality cost.
details: All query heads share a single key/value head, shrinking the KV cache dramatically and speeding up decoding at a small quality cost.

explainer.lead: Multi-query attention has all query heads share a single key/value head, which shrinks the KV cache dramatically and speeds up decoding. It trades a small amount of quality for much cheaper inference.

tiers.eli5: Many people ask questions, but they all read from the same single shared answer sheet instead of each keeping their own copy.
tiers.practitioner: It is used to cut KV-cache memory and accelerate decoding. The pitfall is a modest quality cost relative to full multi-head attention.
tiers.paperLevel: All query heads share one key head and one value head, so the KV cache scales with a single head rather than the number of query heads. The known trade-off is a small quality loss.

explainer.example: During generation, a model with many query heads stores just one key/value pair per position, so the KV cache is far smaller than with per-head key/value pairs.
